output.name: Tirka
output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the sky went up and the ladder did not. Ennu had knotted it that spring from goat gut and whale-rib rungs, and it hung from the cliff-nail like a line off a drying rack. Aun went down it, because he was Aun and wanted to see the bottom. The rungs went on past the last gull; the Stilled Gull, too proud to come down, watched from the west, neck stretched up like a hand asking for rain. The Ray That Flies saw the first rung swing in the east and said nothing. Hesk counted the rungs and did not like the number. Tavo came by laughing and shook the ladder, and it has been knocking since. The Cut End hangs near the foot with a short cord knotted to Aun's wrist, and some say he is still climbing down, one hand under the other. The sailors of the Leeward Reach will not put a boat under it. If you hear a rung knock on a still night, that is not the wind. That is someone who has not reached the bottom yet.
output.finding: Find the Ray That Flies, a bright star, then go west by a hand-span and a little more (about 22°) to reach Tirka in the Unflown.
